newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Central Africa CFA bank cash injections up in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Central Africa CFA bank cash injections up in Dec.

text.p: Commodity marketing seasons in the Central African CFA franc monetary zone led to a rise in Central Bank (BEAC) cash injections and a decrease in member bank deposits in December, the bank's monthly bulletin said.
The volume of total transactions on the monetary market increased to 17.2 billion CFA from 13.8 billion in November.

"The financing of the various marketing seasons in member countries obliged certain credit institutions to turn to the Central Bank, after they had exhausted their own excess reserves," said the bulletin.

In line with this trend, bank deposits at the BEAC were down in December and the average amount deposited for the zone decreased to 65.7 billion CFA, from 67.3 billion in November, 81.8 billion in October and 102.4 billion in September.

According to the bulletin, banks in Cameroon, still incur the highest average daily deposit, which increased 4.1 percent to 32.7 billion CFA in December. This can be traced to a bank which received foreign capital for the purchase of state-rubber company, Hevecam, sold in November to Indonesian group PANWELL.
Banks in Chad also reduced their deposits this month due to an increase in activity in the cotton marketing season.

Interbank market activity went down by nearly 50 percent, from 7.5 billion CFA in November to 3.9 billion in December. Once again, banks in Chad and Gabon were the only ones to register any operations on the interbank market, with volumes of 0.9 and 3.0 billion CFA respectively.
The average interbank rate in December was 6.0089 percent, compared to 5.6208 percent the previous month.
The BEAC money market rates were unchanged with the intervention rate at 9.75 percent and the two to seven day lending rate at 10 percent.
The Central African monetary zone groups six countries in the region -- Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and Chad.
